gaps.fact: Sake bottle sizes: 300 ml, 720 ml and 1.8 L. No chapter, stem or service table gives a sake format (the bottles table stops at wine), so this Court row is wholly uncovered.

Kimoto and Yamahai carry much more umami and pair with bigger, richer meats. The Village chapter's pairing line is general (miso, mushrooms, shellfish, fried food) and c-n3stz04t asks about warming a yamahai, not about the food; no stem matches kimoto or yamahai to rich meat.

The Sake Meter Value runs from about minus 15 to plus 15. The direction is taught and asked (c-2ln0b4lp), and that explanation gives the usual premium band of minus two to plus ten, but the Court's printed range is never given.

The Court's polishing minimums as one table: Daiginjo 50, Ginjo 60, Honjozo 70, Junmai Daiginjo 50, Junmai Ginjo 60. Both chapters print them and the Régionale bank asks ginjo (i-s02d29l7) and daiginjo (i-073qtlea), but no stem keys honjozo's 70 per cent and no Village stem keys any of the five figures (c-1j5mlxff, in Service & Hospitality, asks only which measurement separates the grades).

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 64 (Sake & Spirits, of which 33 are on sake, one of them, i-4jhk1f7c, telling sake from shochu), Village 20 (Sake), 84 in all and 53 on sake. Two more sake stems sit outside the map in Service & Hospitality (c-1j5mlxff, the polishing ratio; c-ly7s66za, a daiginjo served chilled). The Court's Producer/Proprietary Brand and History & Lore rows print both cells blank on page 87 and are not rows here. Coverage is strong: every Court line on ingredients, koji, parallel fermentation, the special grades, nigori, namazake, kimoto and yamahai, tokubetsu and service has a chapter fact and a stem; the Village bank is pitched above the Court (koji rice floor, moromi, namachozo, toji, the US tax and label split) and leaves the Court's own figures to the Régionale bank. Court cells to read with care in our own copy: 'Each sake distillery has its own unique water source' calls a brewery a distillery, which the Codex rightly never does (i-1ead5lc9, the trap 'never distilled'), so an e- question on the row should say brewery; 'Sake is typically 15-22% abv' runs to the legal ceiling for seishu, where the Codex teaches about 15 to 16 per cent at bottling and 17 to 20 for genshu (i-l6nzhe21, i-clxphuq3), both consistent with it. One search spent, on the special designation labelling rules: it found no revision since the National Tax Agency's 2022 amendment, in force from 1 January 2023 and so before the guide's date; no court update logged, and the second search was not spent.
